conventions.convention: The lattice transform uses exp(−ik·n), the torus is R^d/(2πZ)^d with normalized measure (2π)^−d dk, and both Hilbert-space pairings are conjugate-linear in the first variable.
An isolated cluster is a fixed nonempty consecutive eigenvalue block, counted with multiplicity, uniformly separated from its complement. The full-spectrum block has projector I.
The determinant construction accepts C² constant-rank orthogonal projectors with 1 ≤ m ≤ r; the standard increasing wedges are orthonormal and Q = exterior power m of P.
The torus orientation is dk₁∧dk₂, sphere orientation is outward, sphere area is normalized to integral one, and degree is defined by the induced map on integral fundamental classes.
For the projected connection P d, F = P(dP∧dP)P and C(P) = (i/2π)∫tr F. Full AC and Countable Choice are explicit assumptions of the Chern theorem.
For the displayed Pauli matrices, P_s = (I+s n·σ)/2, with s=+1 for the upper band, and C(P_s)=−s deg(n).

The velocity result concerns stationary C² curves of the explicitly adopted effective action, with fixed endpoints. Wave vector has inverse-metre units, q is signed charge, A=i u*du, and Ω=curl A. No approximation error or empirical validity is asserted.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. For a C² constant-rank orthogonal projector P on the oriented two-torus, C(P)=(i/2π)∫tr(P(dP∧dP)P)=⟨c₁(det E_P),[T²]⟩∈Z. C(P_t) is constant for jointly C² fixed-rank projector homotopies; a global C² periodic orthonormal frame implies C(P)=0.
Under Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice, for the stated two-orbital finite-range Bloch Hamiltonian with d nowhere zero, C(P_+)=−deg(n) and C(P_-)=+deg(n), where deg(n)=(1/4π)∫n·(∂₁n×∂₂n) dk₁ dk₂.

Under Countable Choice, H₀ extends uniquely to a bounded self-adjoint H, F₀ extends uniquely to a unitary F, FHF⁻¹ is multiplication by the smooth Hermitian matrix h(k), and a uniformly separated consecutive eigenvalue block has a smooth orthogonal projector locally given by the stated Riesz integral.
For the stated C² projector and C² local orthonormal frame V, the determinant-line connection form in the wedge frame is a=tr(V*dV), and da=tr(V*FV)=tr F.
For the projector of def-nrqmx-determinant-line-projector, Q(x)=exterior power m of P(x) is a C² orthogonal projector of rank one, with range exactly exterior power m of im P(x).
For every smooth n:T²₂π→S² with the stated orientations and normalized sphere area form, ∫n*ω_S²=deg(n)∈Z, where n_*[T²₂π]=deg(n)[S²] in integral homology.
For h_M=sin(k₁)σ₁+sin(k₂)σ₂+(M+cos(k₁)+cos(k₂))σ₃, the gap closes exactly at M=−2,0,2. On the four successive complementary intervals, C(P_-) is 0,+1,−1,0 and C(P_+) has the opposite sign.

concerns.concern: The title claims 'The determinant-line projector is smooth and rank one', but the Definition permits merely C² P and the Statement correctly concludes only C² Q. Smooth means C∞ in def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds. The title's stronger claim is false: on M=R, take m=1, r=2, v(x)=(cos(|x|³),sin(|x|³)) and P=vv*. Then Q=P is C² but not C³ at zero. The same overstatement is repeated in F2 of lem-nrqmx-determinant-curvature-is-trace ('Q is a smooth rank-one orthogonal projector'). The actual proofs require only C² and do not establish smoothing.

alerts.finding: In step 2.1, 'these restrictions form a continuous complex line-bundle isomorphism E_P≅E_Rε and [F6] gives c₁(E_P)=c₁(E_Rε)' applies def-chern-classes-from-the-projective-bundle-relation to E_P without explicitly establishing its numerability. That definition requires a numerable bundle. Local C² frames, compactness, and a finite subordinate partition close the gap immediately; the owned consumer thm-nrqmx-bloch-projector-chern explicitly supplies this argument in step 1.1.
